sweep_summary: Both title-works with stress in the title are Florence Gerdel's word-and-phrase pitch-stress study of Páez: the 1985 English chapter (already held by the project; now scanned in full, printed pp.31-42) and its 1983 Spanish twin in Artículos en Lingüística y Campos Afines 12 (SIL archive 18974, 'Not Available Online'; not in HathiTrust/Google Books/archive.org). The 1983 text is nevertheless in hand: the SIL archives listing for pbb (the Internet Archive 2015) turned up Gerdel's 'Fonología del páez (Revisada 1989)' (SIL 19040, 48 pp, downloaded via the Internet Archive), whose note 13 states that its sections 7-8 were published as Gerdel 1983 and Brend 1985:31-42, and whose bibliography lists the two as one work. All three texts agree with the catalog's 'lexical' coding and its deciding quotations (Gerdel 1973:28 'El acento es contrastable..'; Gerdel 1985:32 root-anchoring): stress is contrastive on shape-identical roots, always within the root for non-verbs, medial in trisyllabic roots, and shifted off the root only for Set B verbs under specific suffixes. Refinements from the 1989 revision: the accompanying tone is now called 'ascendente' (rising) rather than 'alto'; the practical orthography writes the accent only on word-final stress and on accented particles (note 30), implying non-final root stress is the unmarked case; the data are from the Pitayó dialect (note 1). Nothing contradicts the classification; no source states a positional default. Recommend adding Gerdel 1989/1990 (SIL 19040) and Gerdel 1983 (as the Spanish version of 1985) to the per-language bibliography. all look-ups were done by direct downloads (Glottolog, SIL record pages, the Internet Archive, archive.org, Fabre).

new_statements.reading: Páez (Pitayó dialect) has one primary stress per phonological word, realised with rising pitch. Its position is lexically contrastive within roots of identical shape (wála/wakú; ísa/wakú; déwe/pedá) and is anchored to the root rather than to a syllable count: non-verb roots always carry it; trisyllabic roots carry it medially; verb roots fall into Set A (stress stays on the root) and Set B (stress moves to the first formative vowel before four tense-aspect suffixes, or to accented allomorphs of five derivational suffixes; otherwise on the root). The 1989 orthography marks the accent only when it is word-final or on an inherently accented particle, so non-final root stress is the unmarked case, but no positional default is stated in any of the three Gerdel texts. This is a lexical/morphologically anchored system, not a positional (penult) one.

audit.recode_to: No forced reclassify. After re-reading Díaz Montenegro 2019 ch.5, decide between keeping 'lexical' (non-strict, root-anchored; Gerdel's Pitayó stems ísa/déwe vs wakú/pedá/lawéč are genuinely contrastive, and Munchique verbs are ˈσσ or σˈσ with PFV/IPFV shift) and 'morphological' (root = accentogenic unit, affixes inert, aspect marked by stress shift, nominal roots ~98% initial in Munchique). Either way add Díaz 2019:201-213 and Mondelli 2014:28-30 as sources and note the dialect difference (Pitayó vs Munchique). Gordon 2002 'Penult' stays contradicted at word level (kíwe-ga 100, ˈstela=aˀs, ˈkiwa=tʲi), though Gerdel 1985:32 'stems of three syllables do not carry stress on the first or last syllable' plus the disyllabic initial default is probably where a stem-level penult reading came from -- worth saying in the contra note.

sources.note: One primary pitch-stress nucleus per phonological word. Monomorphemic stems show both initial and final placement (ísa, déwe vs wakú, pedá, lawéč, pagáy); trisyllabic stems are stressed medially. In non-verbs the nucleus is always within the root (kápa?, kíwega). Verbs split into Set A (nucleus on the stem) and Set B (nucleus shifts to the first formative vowel before -ç/-ga/-n/-?, or to accented variants of derivational suffixes -sáa, -níi, -káxn, -wá?x, -núu; otherwise on the stem), yielding homophones resolved by context (sec. 2.3.3). sources.quote: [Gerdel 1989 (1990) sec. 7.1, p.24:] La palabra fonológica en páez está marcada por dos rasgos primarios: (1) una pausa potencial en los límites fonológicos, y (2) un núcleo fonológico que conlleva acento primario y tono ascendente. La ubicación principal del núcleo de tono-acento está en la raíz. Sin embargo, cuando ciertos sufijos y partículas que de por sí llevan tono-acento van después de la raíz del verbo, el núcleo fonológico se traslada de la raíz del verbo a otro lugar. [= The phonological word in Páez is marked by two primary features: (1) potential pause at the boundaries and (2) a phonological nucleus bearing primary stress and rising pitch. The main location of the pitch-stress nucleus is the root. However, when certain suffixes and particles that carry pitch-stress of their own follow a verb root, the phonological nucleus moves from the verb root elsewhere.]
